goal: Watch the rug ball stop in different places, share notices and wonders, and start a before-and-after picture chart.
note: Hook and question board; introduce looking, listening and drawing without tasting or sniffing. Start the teacher-led two-minute daily weather chart on school day 1, outside lesson time; keep it all year. K.MD.A.2 is in math unit 3, weeks 9 to 13: bridge by side-by-side tape marks, no numbers.
supplies: large soft balls; masking tape (household stand-in)
safety: rolling: floor in a cleared space, no throwing; choking: balls large enough not to be a choking hazard
opens: Hook and teaching first: three volunteers roll one ball from the same start tape and the teacher marks each stop with tape, one roll gets a sideways tap and turns, and the big question is asked with no cause given; the teacher then models a safe roll, the floor-only and wait-behind-the-line rules, and the three-box strip (before, touch, after)
holds: the teacher holds the class picture chart and the question board; each child holds a three-box strip
by_hand: rolling one ball, drawing a before, touch and after strip, saying notices and wonders aloud
exit: s01-X1: touch the picture of what made a cushion slide (invented for practice)
shows: Watch the rug ball stop in different places = s01-X1 s01-E5; share notices and wonders = s01-X1; start a before-and-after picture chart = s01-X1

goal: Plan and carry out a gentle-push and strong-push comparison using the same ball and starting place.
note: Children help choose what changes and what stays the same; cause-effect introduced. Teacher records dots for stopping places; only strength changes.
supplies: large soft balls; masking tape (household stand-in)
safety: rolling: floor in a cleared space, no throwing; choking: balls large enough not to be a choking hazard
opens: Teaching first: Pip guesses a harder push goes farther; the class says what to change (how hard), what to keep (same ball, same start tape, same way) and what to watch (the start and where it stops), and the teacher rolls gently and then harder and lays a dot strip beside the lane
holds: the teacher holds the chart and the keep, change, watch cards; each child holds a guess drawing and a dot strip
by_hand: rolling gently and then harder, marking dots on a strip, laying strips side by side to say nearer, farther or about the same
exit: s01-X2: say what changes and what stays the same in a new push test of a pram (invented for practice)
shows: Plan = s01-X2 s01-E1; carry out a gentle-push and strong-push comparison using the same ball and starting place = s01-X2 s01-E2

goal: Compare gentle and stronger pulls on a box and describe its motion before and after.
note: Candidate kept: oral before-and-after descriptions embedded in days 2 to 7, zero added days; only pull strength changes.
supplies: light cardboard box (household stand-in); short thick string; masking tape
safety: pulling: floor in a cleared space, no throwing; string: teacher attaches short lengths, no loops around bodies; observation: no tasting or sniffing unknowns
opens: Teaching first: does pulling work like pushing; the teacher pulls a box by its string gently and then harder from the same start and the class says what started and how
holds: the teacher holds the chart; each child holds a before and after strip with a dictated label
by_hand: pulling the box gently and then harder from the same start, drawing the box before and after, dictating a label
exit: s01-X3: say which of two pulls moved a new wagon farther, gentle or stronger (invented for practice)
shows: Compare gentle and stronger pulls on a box = s01-X3 s01-E3; describe its motion before and after = s01-X3 s01-E3

goal: Keep push strength similar and change its direction to explain the ball turning.
note: Direction alone varies; use tape marks as the math bridge, not numerical distance.
supplies: large soft balls; masking tape (household stand-in)
safety: rolling: floor in a cleared space, no throwing; choking: balls large enough not to be a choking hazard
opens: Plan: the class applies the one-change plan; keep the ball and a similar slow push, change which way, with two tape X marks, and the group says what to keep, change and watch
holds: the teacher holds the chart; each child holds a path strip
by_hand: pushing the ball slowly from the side toward each X, marking the paths on a strip, watching the box pulled toward each X
exit: s01-X4: say what touched a new ball to make it turn toward a mark (invented for practice)
shows: Keep push strength similar = s01-X4 s01-E4; change its direction to explain the ball turning = s01-X4 s01-E4

goal: Observe a hand stopping a rolling ball and two large balls bumping, then revise the motion chart.
note: Contact pushes change motion when objects collide; roll slowly, keep fingers clear of collisions. For 20-minute periods only, this is one of the unit's four observation-window days (5/6/8/9): ten minutes essential teaching, ten new-case evidence today; closing days add twenty and ten evidence minutes, then ten response minutes. Split group parts at day boundaries, one per-child record; full parts are in the closing rows.
supplies: large soft balls; masking tape (household stand-in)
safety: rolling: floor in a cleared space, no throwing; choking: balls large enough not to be a choking hazard
opens: Teaching first: the teacher stops a rolling ball with a flat hand and rolls one ball into another resting ball, Pip asks whether touching can change something already moving, and the class says what changed
holds: the teacher holds the chart and the order cards; each child holds a touch strip
by_hand: rolling one ball into a resting ball and past a resting ball with a gap, drawing the touch and the change, putting order cards in order
exit: s01-X5: say what happened to a resting bus when a rolling bus touched it (invented for practice)
shows: Observe a hand stopping a rolling ball and two large balls bumping = s01-X5 s01-E5; then revise the motion chart = s01-X5 s01-E5

goal: Plan another one-change comparison and use observations to revise the class cause-effect chart.
note: Children select strength or direction, never both; scientists find out by looking and testing, and may use different methods; no magnets. For 20-minute periods only, this is one of the unit's four observation-window days (5/6/8/9): ten minutes essential teaching, ten new-case evidence today; closing days add twenty and ten evidence minutes, then ten response minutes. Split group parts at day boundaries, one per-child record; full parts are in the closing rows.
supplies: large soft balls; masking tape (household stand-in)
safety: rolling: floor in a cleared space, no throwing; choking: balls large enough not to be a choking hazard
opens: Plan: each group picks one change by pointing at a card, how hard or which way and never both, and sets what to keep and watch; groups may choose different tests
holds: the teacher holds the chart; each group holds a group card
by_hand: making the two settings of the group's change with a ball, marking the picture chart, telling one mark
exit: s01-X6: say Pip's next one-change test of a sled and what stays the same (invented for practice)
shows: Plan another one-change comparison = s01-E1; use observations to revise the class cause-effect chart = s01-X6 s01-E6

goal: Would a loaded box respond to gentle and stronger pulls in the same way as the empty box?
note: Compare pulls on a box carrying one large soft block; keep its load fixed while varying pull strength. Explain before and after from marked stopping places. Fold into day 6 as a six-minute second case, replacing duplicate trials.
supplies: light cardboard box (household stand-in); short thick string; masking tape; large soft block
safety: pulling: floor in a cleared space, no throwing; string: teacher attaches short lengths, no loops around bodies; observation: no tasting or sniffing unknowns
opens: Guess: practice, nothing new; would a box carrying one large soft block respond to gentle and stronger pulls as the empty box did, and each child draws a guess
holds: the teacher holds the chart and the day 3 strips; each child holds a guess drawing and a strip
by_hand: pulling the loaded box gently and then harder, marking the stop, laying strips beside the day 3 strips
exit: s01-X7: say whether a new loaded cart moved like the empty cart for a gentle and a harder pull (invented for practice)
shows: Would a loaded box respond to gentle and stronger pulls in the same way as the empty box = s01-X7 s01-E3

goal: Observe each child planning and carrying out a new contact-motion comparison and explaining the result.
note: End-of-unit observation, first group rotation; new objects and layout. Each child compares strong and gentle pushes AND pulls, and changed direction in separate one-variable trials, describes starting, stopping, speed and turning, and explains collision evidence with the revised chart. Complete remaining children on day 9. Six groups of five for 30 children: four groups at seven minutes today, two groups at seven minutes next day; two minutes set-up today, six minutes set-up/record completion next day, then ten-minute response. Each child has an own picture mat and checklist entry; parallel card/drawing responses cover every part and each gives one brief spoken why per code. Teacher observes each child's planning/action where required, not only a spokesperson. Others independently draw the rug-ball anchor and mark before/after positions.
supplies: large soft balls; masking tape (household stand-in); light cardboard box; short thick string; individual picture response mats; crayons
safety: rolling: floor in a cleared space, no throwing; choking: balls large enough not to be a choking hazard; string: short teacher-attached lengths, no body loops
opens: Set-up: five lanes with five balls, boxes and strings and mats in a new layout, fitted eye protection on everyone present
holds: each child holds an own picture response mat; the teacher holds the record sheet
by_hand: planning with cards, pushing and pulling in matched pairs, tapping from the side, marking the mat, saying one reason
exit: END
shows: Observe each child planning = s01-E1; carrying out a new contact-motion comparison = s01-E2 s01-E3 s01-E4 s01-E5; explaining the result = s01-E6
check_min: Set-up 2; Group 1 observed 7; Group 2 observed 7; Group 3 observed 7; Group 4 observed 7

goal: Complete remaining motion observations, reteach from the record and hear a fresh explanation.
note: Same complete observation scope as day 8 for remaining children. Unit 1 response occurs once in the final ten minutes, with a fresh one-change comparison; no next-unit readiness check. Use the six-group plan begun yesterday; retain each child's single record, no second collection. Others continue the same named independent task.
supplies: large soft balls; masking tape (household stand-in); light cardboard box; short thick string; individual picture response mats; crayons
safety: rolling: floor in a cleared space, no throwing; choking: balls large enough not to be a choking hazard; string: short teacher-attached lengths, no body loops
opens: Set-up as on day 8, then the last two groups are observed; the teacher completes the records, reads feedback aloud, repairs with the largest error group and asks two fresh-case questions
holds: the teacher holds the record sheet; each child holds an own picture response mat
by_hand: the day 8 tasks for the remaining children, finishing mats, touching picture cards on a fresh case
exit: s01-X9 and s01-X9b: touch the pictures for a fair check of a push and for what moved the cloth (invented for practice, not scored)
shows: Complete remaining motion observations = s01-E1 s01-E2 s01-E3 s01-E4 s01-E5 s01-E6; reteach from the record = s01-X9 s01-X9b; hear a fresh explanation = s01-X9 s01-X9b

goal: Meet the morning coat pile and afternoon change, then read the class weather pictures for a question.
note: Hook, question board and initial pattern chart; retrieve unit 1 recording and cause-effect inside the day. Math K.MD.B.3 is in unit 2, weeks 4 to 9: match picture squares, count groups up to ten together, teacher labels larger totals.
supplies: picture cards (no-kit); class picture chart
safety: none
opens: Hook and teaching first: two photographs of the class coat hooks, morning and afternoon, beside that day's row of the class weather chart, with the big question asked and no answer given; a short retrieval of the unit 1 three-box strip; then Pip and the teacher read one dated chart row (date square, morning picture, afternoon picture, warmth mark) and say morning, afternoon, warmer and cooler
holds: the teacher holds the coat photographs, the class picture chart and the question board; each group holds a table copy of five dated rows; each child holds a blank picture card to draw on
by_hand: pointing to one thing noticed in a chart row, drawing the sky to look at to find out what changed, placing the first school-day squares in rows
exit: s02-X10: touch the question that two pictures of one place, morning and afternoon, can help answer (another observer's record)
shows: Meet the morning coat pile = s02-X10; afternoon change = s02-X10; then read the class weather pictures for a question = s02-X10

goal: Plan morning and afternoon weather looks and compare warmer and cooler across several days.
note: Candidate kept: one day for the small relative-temperature investigation, using the daily routine for repeat looks. Never teach cooler mornings as a rule without reading actual records; no degrees. Teacher saves fall photographs of a sidewalk weed and an animal-dug hole for unit 4.
supplies: class weather picture chart; drawing paper
safety: outdoor observation: stay in sight, touch nothing unknown; sunlight: never look at the sun; weather: observe indoors if conditions are unsafe
opens: Teaching first: Pip asks how to find out whether the afternoon is warmer, the class chooses the plan cards (keep the place, keep how we look, change the time, watch the sky and the feel) and the teacher models the morning mark
holds: the teacher holds the class weather picture chart and the plan cards; each child holds a look sheet
by_hand: choosing plan cards, marking the sky card and a start dot on the own look sheet at the taped spot
exit: s02-X11a and s02-X11b: touch the plan that looks at the same place at two times, and say which of two days in an invented record had a warmer afternoon than morning (invented for practice)
shows: Plan morning and afternoon weather looks = s02-X11a; compare warmer and cooler across several days = s02-X11b

goal: Is the slide or bench warmer at afternoon recess than it was in the morning?
note: Take a second morning/afternoon look using the chart words and record what actually happens. No fixed cooler-morning answer. Fold into day 11 as a six-minute second case, replacing duplicate chart turns.
supplies: class weather picture chart; drawing paper
safety: outdoor observation: stay in sight, touch nothing unknown; sunlight: never look at the sun; weather: observe indoors if conditions are unsafe; hot surfaces: teacher checks first, students touch briefly with the back of a hand
opens: Practice: read yesterday's afternoon mark beside the morning start dots and say the plan again with the cards (keep the bench and its sun or shade, change the time, watch the feel); nothing new is taught
holds: the teacher holds the morning dot, the hand wipes and the pattern sheet; each child holds an own dot on the bench sheet
by_hand: laying the back of one hand on the safe bench for a few seconds and marking cool or warm, drawing the bench with sun or shade
exit: s02-X12: touch the time when an invented bench was warmer (invented for practice)
shows: Is the slide or bench warmer at afternoon recess than it was in the morning? = s02-X12

goal: Arrange complete daily records in picture rows and count selected weather groups with support.
note: Math bridge until unit 2 ends on school day 44: match squares to compare rows, children count at most ten, teacher counts and labels larger totals. Weather categories can overlap, so counts need not sum to days.
supplies: picture cards (no-kit); class picture chart
safety: none
opens: Teaching first: the teacher and Pip put five dated class squares into rows (sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy), lay two rows side by side to see which is longer, touch each square once and say the last number, and the teacher says any total over ten
holds: the teacher holds the demonstration rows; each group holds a set of five squares and a row mat
by_hand: sorting squares into rows, touching each square once and saying the last number
exit: s02-X13: touch each rainy day once among five days of another observer's record and say how many
shows: Arrange complete daily records in picture rows = s02-X13; count selected weather groups with support = s02-X13

goal: Count the sunny, cloudy, rainy and windy days in our first complete month and revise the pattern chart.
note: Read the dated live class record from school days 1 to about 20; count selected groups to ten with support, teacher labels larger totals. Match picture rows and keep overlapping categories separate. Only for a late-starting class use a real dated picture record from elsewhere, labelled as another observer's data; never translate missing categories from temperature or rain tables.
supplies: class weather picture chart; drawing paper
safety: none
opens: Set-up: the teacher reads the month's dates in order and names the gaps; gaps stay gaps
holds: the teacher holds the picture graph and the pattern sheet; each group holds a table copy of the live record from the first school day with its gaps
by_hand: sorting the month's squares into four rows, counting a row each, filling the class graph from the group rows
exit: s02-X14a, s02-X14b and s02-X14c: touch each rainy day once in a whole month of another observer's record, say whether a day in two rows is one day or two, and touch the longer of two matched rows
shows: Count the sunny, cloudy, rainy and windy days in our first complete month = s02-X14a s02-X14b s02-X14c; revise the pattern chart = s02-X14b s02-X14c

goal: Meet a calm forecast of indoor recess and ask why people need weather forecasts.
note: Local severe weather: model asking for information, then each child asks. ELA SL.K.3 is in unit 1 through school day 34, overlapping: bridge with a teacher-modelled question and sentence starter. Focus on helpers, no disaster retellings or frightening images; no questions about coats or home heating. For 20-minute periods only, this is one of the unit's four observation-window days (15/17/18/19): ten minutes essential teaching, ten new-case evidence today; closing days add twenty and ten evidence minutes, then ten response minutes. Split group parts at day boundaries, one per-child record; full parts are in the closing rows.
supplies: calm forecast picture sequence (no-kit); Curio Class read-aloud picture pages
safety: none
opens: Hook and teaching first: the read-aloud Before We Go Out (the story is invented, the weather page is real), then the teacher models one I-want-to-find-out question about the first forecast page with the four question cards and the page, plan, indoor recess strip
holds: the teacher holds the forecast pages, the strip and the read-aloud; each child holds question cards
by_hand: asking one I-want-to-find-out question in pairs, pointing to the picture that could answer it, putting a question the page cannot answer on the not-on-this-page card
exit: s02-X15: say what you want to find out from a new real forecast page for one day in June
shows: Meet a calm forecast of indoor recess = s02-X15; ask why people need weather forecasts = s02-X15

goal: What can a second calm regional forecast tell us that our first source did not?
note: Ask a new question of a different supplied forecast source about local severe weather and preparations; retain the modelled question and calm-image choice. Fold into day 15 as a six-minute second-source case, replacing duplicate partner turns.
supplies: second calm regional forecast picture sequence (no-kit); drawing paper
safety: none
opens: Second source: the teacher shows the discussion page for the same July day (the timing, and a picture of earlier storms moving away) and asks what this page can tell us that the first one did not; practice only
holds: the teacher holds the chain on the wall chart; each group holds the second page; each child holds question cards
by_hand: asking a new question the first page could not answer and pointing to the picture that answers it
exit: s02-X16: say a question the second real page can answer and the first could not (real pages for one day in June)
shows: What can a second calm regional forecast tell us that our first source did not? = s02-X16

goal: Ask how a local weather pattern helps forecasters warn people and use the answer to choose safe community actions.
note: Use a sourced calm picture-record comparison: some severe-weather types occur more often in this region than elsewhere. Each child asks a question and obtains the answer from supplied records/media; forecasters combine observed patterns and current information to predict danger so communities prepare and respond. Worked case: labeled Denver and Seattle thunderstorm records (a Colorado example; naming each school's own regional hazard is an open plan question); no probability or atmospheric mechanism, frightening images or personal disaster accounts. For 20-minute periods only, this is one of the unit's four observation-window days (15/17/18/19): ten minutes essential teaching, ten new-case evidence today; closing days add twenty and ten evidence minutes, then ten response minutes. Split group parts at day boundaries, one per-child record; full parts are in the closing rows.
supplies: dated regional weather picture records (no-kit); calm forecast picture sequence (no-kit); Curio Class read-aloud picture pages
safety: none
opens: Model: the teacher lays Denver's and Seattle's July thunder-report squares side by side with the interval on the caption (Denver seventeen, said by the teacher; Seattle none) and says the squares count days with thunder reported at a station, not damage
holds: the teacher holds the chain and the regional record squares; each group holds table copies of the squares; each child holds action cards
by_hand: asking the records a question (which place, how many, when) and pointing to the answer, choosing action cards, drawing the four-box chain
exit: s02-X17a and s02-X17b: say a question to ask the August rows, and say when to plan indoor play on a real page for one day in June
shows: Ask how a local weather pattern helps forecasters warn people = s02-X17a; use the answer to choose safe community actions = s02-X17b

goal: Observe every child sharing counted daily and monthly weather patterns from an unfamiliar record.
note: End-of-unit weather observation for every child: observe/interpret and share daily AND monthly patterns, count a selected whole-number weather group up to ten with support, compare monthly picture rows and actual morning/afternoon relative warmth. Six groups at four minutes, six minutes set-up/transitions. Others independently sort familiar weather pictures. Forecast performance is day 19, not another full performance today. Each of 30 children has an own picture mat and checklist entry; six groups of five, parallel pointing/card/drawing responses and one brief spoken why per code. Record each child, never just a spokesperson. No second collection of an already completed part.
supplies: picture cards (no-kit); class picture chart; unfamiliar forecast picture sequence (no-kit); individual picture response mats; crayons
safety: none
opens: Set-up: six table sets, thirty weather response mats and crayons; the others sort familiar weather pictures
holds: each child holds an own weather response mat; the teacher holds the record sheet
by_hand: pointing to weather pictures, touching each rainy day once and saying the last number, matching two month rows, saying one reason
exit: END
shows: Observe every child sharing counted daily = s02-W1a s02-W1b s02-W2; monthly weather patterns from an unfamiliar record = s02-W3a s02-W3b
check_min: Set-up 2; Group 1 observed 4; Group 2 observed 4; Group 3 observed 4; Group 4 observed 4; Group 5 observed 4; Group 6 observed 4; Change-overs and packing 4

goal: Observe every child asking for forecast information and explaining prediction, preparation and response.
note: End-of-unit forecast observation for every child: ask a question, obtain the answer from supplied calm media, connect regional hazard likelihood and observed weather patterns to prediction, then community preparation AND response. Six groups at three minutes, two minutes set-up and ten response minutes once, responding also to day 18 weather gaps. Others independently sort familiar weather pictures. Read the live two-month chart together without collecting day 18 evidence again; school day 44 provides about two months. Only a late start needs another observer's labelled dated picture records; no invented categories or private disaster accounts. Each of 30 children has an own picture mat and checklist entry; six groups of five, parallel pointing/card/drawing responses and one brief spoken why per code. Record each child, never just a spokesperson. No second collection of an already completed part.
supplies: picture cards (no-kit); class picture chart; unfamiliar forecast picture sequence (no-kit); individual picture response mats; crayons
safety: none
opens: Set-up as on day 18, then six groups of three minutes: each child asks a question of an unfamiliar forecast page, touches the answer, and touches what the school does before and during the storm; the live two-month chart is read as review
holds: each child holds an own forecast response mat; the teacher holds the record sheet and the caption strips
by_hand: asking aloud, touching pictures, drawing, revising up to two captions
exit: s02-X19a and s02-X19b: touch the question a real June page can answer and what the school does before the storm (not scored)

goal: Watch the ramp ball miss the tower and ask what needs to change before proposing a solution.
note: Hook and question board; retrieve unit 1 contact pushes and unit 2 result charts inside the day. ELA SL.K.3 unit 1 ends school day 34, before today. Introduce design-cycle: problem, try an idea, test it. Math comparison in unit 3 may still be developing: tape marks and reached/not reached bridge.
supplies: large soft balls; masking tape (household stand-in); cardboard ramps (household stand-in); books; large blocks; cardboard bumpers
safety: rolling: floor in a cleared space, no throwing; choking: balls large enough not to be a choking hazard; ramps: on the floor, books stacked low

holds: the teacher holds the ramp, the balls, the design-cycle chart and the path model; each child holds a ramp sheet and crayons

exit: s03-X20: say what needs to change in a new picture of a ball stopped short of a tower of cups, before any fix (invented for practice)

goal: Ask questions, observe trials and gather information to state the ramp problem in one sentence.

goal: Build a low ramp solution and record whether the ball reaches the target distance as intended.
